text:
If this were $200 it'd sell like hotcakes. 8 GB isn't really hard to manage if you actually put effort into tweaking the graphical settings related to shadows and lighting which is what robs your fps the most with the least visual fidelity improvement. An 8 GB card can still do anything at 1080p with max textures with everything else on medium and it'll look fine unless it's a poorly optimized piece of garbage like black myth wukong. That game has no business running that "shittily." 

This isn't me advocating for/saying 8 GB is fine or enough...but if you open your brain for a millisecond you'll notice there's still a massive market for these cards and it's for the people who don't want to give someone a ton of money that's also willing to tweak their settings and settle for 1080p 60 fps. 

There are a lot of poor ass people who have no money that work all day that won't mind spending $250 to be able to play any game they want at 1080p with their friends. People like this already eat the slop of the world, they don't care about how good their shadows look in game. Poor people have to navigate the world differently and one of the things we do is lower the shadows and lighting effects. It's like defaulting to the cheaper gas when you fill up at the pump, same goes here. We're already used to turning things down. It's always been like this with low end cards. None of this behavior is new, everyone is just distracted by VRAM which isn't the big picture.

text:
@khawajarashid7799  The OLED TV definitely is improving your picture, yeah. The PS5 isn't all that powerful though, the RX 6600XT gets better performance than it, and Playstation/Xbox use AMD hardware these days so it's a pretty direct comparison. 

It relies heavily on upscaling just to hit 60 FPS on around medium settings, depending on the game. The only games the PS5 can natively do in 4K are very old ones or ones with 2D or very simple 3D graphics. Quality mode on demanding/poorly optimised games leads to around 30 FPS, and it looks pretty rough in motion if you're used to 60+ FPS. 


With PC I'd take a 1440p OLED monitor any day over a 4K IPS. But there's still a noticeable difference between consoles and high-end PCs. My PC only has RX 6800 and at native 1440p High settings on Silent Hill 2 Remake it gets around 70-90 FPS. That's a clear improvement in both the visual quality and smoothness.

Not that I think 4K is even that big of a deal. The performance hit is pretty significant for a marginal improvement to the clarity of the visuals. a better TV/monitor and higher graphics settings will make a much bigger impact on the image. The real reason to go with PC is the long-term value. A low or mid-range PC will cost similar or a moderate amount more than a console, but emulation, free online, better sales, modding and more adds up to make PC less expensive in the long run while also giving you more freedom.
